assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order, with compensated moments yet spin-split bands set by crystal symmetry. It rests on spin-group symmetry analysis combined with first-principles electronic-structure calculations, so it is a clean example of theory that changed how magnetism is classified. It also opens a distinct route to spintronics without net magnetization. Importance, originality and conceptual clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: The 2019-2022 symmetry classification and the anomalous-Hall and spin-splitting predictions are credited to Šmejkal, Jungwirth and Sinova, with Jungwirth as the long-time leader of the programme. The three-person configuration fits well. Related earlier symmetry-based work by other groups (for example Hayami, Yanagi and Kusunose, Yuan and Zunger) may raise priority questions.
assessment.maturity: Spin-split bands have been observed by ARPES and related probes in MnTe and CrSb, and anomalous Hall signals were reported in several materials, so independent confirmation exists. The field is still young and device relevance is not yet demonstrated, so some may call recognition early. For a new magnetic class with experimental verification I consider it reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Priority relative to earlier symmetry-based proposals by other groups is not fully settled.
Which reported materials are truly altermagnets, and the size of the effect, is still being established; my recollection of the experimental timeline is not independently verified.
Practical technological payoff is still prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory provides a controlled non-perturbative treatment of strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions and in practice the standard route to the Mott transition and correlated materials. Combined with density functional theory (DFT+DMFT) it underlies quantitative modelling of real compounds. Its influence across condensed matter and materials science is deep and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar's mapping onto an impurity problem, and the Müller-Hartmann and Georges-Kotliar-Krauth-Rozenberg work form the core. Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt is a defensible trio, though Metzner, Rozenberg and Krauth, and Müller-Hartmann (deceased), complicate credit and the list is restricted to the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of use, with extensive benchmarking against experiments (spectroscopy, transport, cold-atom simulation). The interpretation is stable and the recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the originators beyond three people is genuinely contested.
Limits of DMFT for low-dimensional systems and the accuracy of DFT+DMFT for specific materials remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and later coherent tunnelling in MgO barriers, enabled hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It is a quantum-transport effect of clear scientific content with very large technological impact, a natural successor to the giant-magnetoresistance prize of 2007.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin led the optimization of high-TMR MgO junctions with Yuasa and Djayaprawira, whose work is not in the supplied credit. The three supplied names support a fair prize but the MgO contribution is only partly captured.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than two decades of commercial use and multiple independent confirmations. The physics, including spin-dependent tunnelling and symmetry filtering, is well understood. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the GMR prize could be judged as lowering novelty.
Credit for the MgO breakthrough involves people absent from the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a field in which band topology and spin-orbit coupling yield protected edge and surface states. The theoretical prediction (Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) followed by the HgTe transport observation is a textbook prediction-confirmation sequence. Impact on materials theory and electronic-structure practice is large.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are decisive for the Z2 theory; Molenkamp led the HgTe observation in 2007. Hasan's 3D topological insulator ARPES work is also important, and Bernevig, Zhang and Fu are not in the supplied credit. I choose Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the cleanest theory-plus-experiment trio, but the four-name list shows a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups for two decades. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions, so this is a distinct but related topic. Timely, though practical applications remain limited.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Zhang (deceased), Bernevig, Fu and Hasan makes any trio contestable.
Relation to the 2016 prize and to the quantum anomalous Hall effect candidates affects how narrowly to frame it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at a magic twist angle, and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moiré materials. This is a striking case where band-structure theory preceded and guided a major experimental advance, and it provides a tunable platform for correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key prediction in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero led the 2018 experiments with Cao and colleagues, a student whose role is not in the supplied credit. The three-person set is natural, but junior contributors and other theory groups (Santos, Peres, Lopes dos Santos) complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Since 2018 many groups have reproduced the correlated phases, though sample-dependence and the mechanism of superconductivity are unresolved. Interpretation is not stable enough yet, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the origin of correlated states are still debated.
Sample variability and the priority claims of earlier theory work on twisted bilayers.
Dependence on later moiré discoveries (including fractional Chern states) for the full legacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are the strongest permanent magnets known and underpin electric vehicles, wind turbines, motors and data storage. The discovery combined materials exploration with understanding of the Nd2Fe14B phase, whose intrinsic magnetic properties arise from rare-earth 4f and transition-metal 3d interplay, the type of problem addressed by electronic-structure theory. The importance is very high, though as a materials discovery its fit to a physics prize is a judgement.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa at Sumitomo (rapid-quenching and sintered magnets) and Croat at General Motors (melt-spun magnets) independently announced the compound in 1983-84. Both are credited and the two-person configuration is natural, though Koon, Herbst and others at other laboratories contributed to the structure and understanding.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of industrial use and thorough characterization. Recognition is, if anything, long overdue; the main question is scientific fit rather than maturity.
uncertainties: Whether the prize committee views this as sufficiently fundamental physics rather than materials engineering.
Allocation between Sagawa and Croat, and roles of others at the discovery stage, from my memory only.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate in 1995 and developed the theory of analogue and digital quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions. The proposal turned experiments into a route to quantum computing and many-body simulation, and its influence on the field is large.
assessment.attribution: The two-person credit is clean and natural. Experimental implementations by Wineland and Blatt groups were already partly recognized by the 2012 prize, so credit allocation to theory is coherent. No unresolved allocation within the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally validated for decades in ion and atom platforms, though the quantum computing promise remains unfulfilled. The simulation line is mature, the computing line still unfolding.
uncertainties: Part of the field has already been recognized in the 2012 and 2022 prizes, so novelty relative to those is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Angle-resolved photoemission is the direct probe of band structure and many-body spectral functions in solids, and its high-resolution development transformed studies of cuprates and other quantum materials. As someone who works on calculated and measured spectra I value the link between theory and spectroscopy, though this is a method with many contributors.
assessment.attribution: Credit for ARPES is spread over many groups and instrument developers, including those working on synchrotron beamlines, so three names may not capture decisive contributions. Campuzano, Shen and Johnson are significant but a fair scope and boundaries of the invention are unclear.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted technique with stable interpretation. Recognition would be timely as a method, but the prize-defining discovery is not obvious.
uncertainties: Method versus discovery: unclear which specific achievement would be cited.
Contributions of other developers of high-resolution ARPES, and of the Fermi-surface and band-mapping tradition, may be omitted.
